_source.reason: AES with 256-bit keys provides ~128-bit post-quantum security (Grover halving)
_source.migration: Upgrade all AES-128 usages to AES-256. AES-256-GCM is the recommended mode.

variants.reason: AES-128 provides only ~64-bit post-quantum security — insufficient

_source.reason: ChaCha20 uses 256-bit keys — provides ~128-bit post-quantum security
_source.migration: No migration needed. ChaCha20 is already quantum-resistant.

_source.reason: AEAD with 256-bit key — Grover-safe with strong authentication
_source.migration: No migration needed. This is a recommended AEAD cipher.
Consider migrating to ChaCha20-Poly1305 for authenticated encryption.

_source.reason: 256-bit block cipher, Grover-safe but not widely deployed
_source.migration: Replace with AES-256-GCM for better hardware acceleration and ecosystem support.

_source.reason: 256-bit block cipher, conservative design but slow
_source.migration: Replace with AES-256-GCM for better performance and ecosystem support.

_source.reason: 64-bit block size — vulnerable to birthday attacks (Sweet32). Not recommended.
_source.migration: Replace immediately with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

_source.reason: 256-bit cipher, Grover-safe. Less common than AES.
_source.migration: Replace with AES-256-GCM for wider ecosystem support unless regulatory requirements mandate Camellia.
No urgent migration. Consider AES-256-GCM for global interoperability.

_source.reason: 112-bit effective key, 64-bit block — vulnerable to Sweet32 and NIST-deprecated since 2023
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace all 3DES usage with AES-256-GCM immediately. This is deprecated by NIST SP 800-131A Rev 2.

_source.reason: 56-bit key — brute-forceable in hours. Completely broken.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace all DES usage with AES-256-GCM immediately.

_source.reason: Multiple cryptographic weaknesses. Prohibited by RFC 7465.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace all RC4 usage with AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

_source.reason: Weak cipher with effective key length attacks.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace with AES-256-GCM.

_source.reason: 128-bit key but outdated design with known weaknesses in reduced rounds
_source.migration: Replace with AES-256-GCM.
Replace with AES-256-GCM.

_source.reason: Authenticated encryption mode — recommended for all block ciphers
_source.migration: No migration needed. GCM is the recommended mode.

_source.reason: Vulnerable to padding oracle attacks if not implemented carefully. Not AEAD.
_source.migration: Replace CBC with GCM or CCM mode for authenticated encryption.

_source.reason: Secure stream mode but requires separate MAC. Prefer GCM for built-in authentication.
_source.migration: Pair with HMAC, or switch to GCM/CCM for built-in authentication.

_source.reason: Authenticated encryption mode. Good alternative to GCM.
_source.migration: No urgent migration. GCM is slightly preferred for parallelism.

_source.reason: INSECURE: Leaks plaintext patterns. Never use for encryption.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace ECB with GCM, CCM, or CTR+HMAC immediately.

_source.reason: 256-bit output provides ~128-bit collision resistance post-quantum (Grover halving)
_source.migration: Consider SHA-384 or SHA3-256 for higher post-quantum security margin.
No migration needed. Excellent quantum-resistant hash.
No migration needed. Strongest SHA-2 variant.

_source.reason: 224-bit output — only ~112-bit post-quantum collision resistance. Marginal.
_source.migration: Upgrade to SHA-256 or SHA-384 for better quantum resistance margin.

_source.reason: SHA-3 family, 256-bit output, different construction from SHA-2 (Keccak sponge)
_source.migration: No migration needed. Excellent quantum-resistant hash.

_source.reason: SHA-3 family, 384-bit output — strong post-quantum collision resistance
_source.migration: No migration needed.

_source.reason: SHA-3 family, 512-bit output — strongest SHA-3 variant
_source.migration: No migration needed.

_source.reason: Modern hash function, up to 512-bit output. Grover-resistant.
_source.migration: No migration needed. BLAKE2 is a strong modern choice.

_source.reason: Latest BLAKE variant, 256-bit output with Merkle tree parallelism
_source.migration: No migration needed.
No migration needed. Consider using standardised SHA-3 interface.
Consider SHAKE256 for higher post-quantum security margin.
No migration needed.

_source.reason: 160-bit output — only ~80-bit post-quantum collision resistance. Obsolete.
_source.migration: Replace with SHA-256 or SHA3-256.
Replace with SHA-512 or SHA3-512 for wider ecosystem support.

_source.reason: BROKEN: Collision attacks are trivial. CVE-2004-2761.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace all MD5 usage. Use SHA-256 for checksums, SHA-384+ for security.

_source.reason: BROKEN: Even weaker than MD5. Collision in seconds.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace immediately with SHA-256 or SHA-384.

_source.reason: BROKEN: Practical collision attacks demonstrated (SHAttered, 2017). NIST deprecated.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace all SHA-1 usage with SHA-256 or SHA-384. Already prohibited for signatures by NIST.

_source.reason: HMAC security depends on underlying hash. HMAC-SHA256+ is Grover-resistant.
_source.migration: Ensure HMAC uses SHA-256 or stronger. Avoid HMAC-MD5 and HMAC-SHA1.

_source.reason: CMAC security depends on underlying cipher (AES-CMAC is Grover-safe).
_source.migration: Ensure CMAC uses AES-256.

_source.reason: Used with ChaCha20 for authenticated encryption. Post-quantum secure.
_source.migration: No migration needed when used as ChaCha20-Poly1305.

_source.reason: KDF security depends on hash and iteration count. Adequate with SHA-256 + high iterations.
_source.migration: Consider Argon2id for new designs. If keeping PBKDF2, use SHA-256 with ≥600,000 iterations (OWASP 2024).

_source.reason: Memory-hard KDF — stronger than PBKDF2 against hardware attacks
_source.migration: Consider Argon2id for new designs. scrypt is acceptable for existing systems.

_source.reason: Winner of Password Hashing Competition. Best-in-class KDF.
_source.migration: No migration needed. Argon2id is the recommended KDF.

_source.reason: Adaptive password hashing. Adequate but limited to 72-byte input.
_source.migration: For new systems, prefer Argon2id. bcrypt is acceptable for existing password storage.

_source.reason: Key derivation function. Security depends on underlying hash (HKDF-SHA256+ is safe).
_source.migration: Ensure HKDF uses SHA-256 or stronger.

_source.reason: QUANTUM VULNERABLE: Broken by Shor's algorithm. All RSA key sizes will be insecure.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace RSA with ML-KEM (FIPS 203) for key exchange and ML-DSA (FIPS 204) for signatures. Use hybrid schemes during transition.

variants.reason: RSA-2048 is current minimum — will be broken by quantum computers
RSA-3072 — slightly more time before quantum break, still vulnerable

_source.reason: QUANTUM VULNERABLE: Broken by Shor's algorithm on elliptic curves.
_source.migration: Replace with ML-DSA (Dilithium) for signatures. Use hybrid ECDSA+ML-DSA during transition.

_source.reason: QUANTUM VULNERABLE: ECDH key exchange broken by Shor's algorithm.
_source.migration: Replace with ML-KEM (Kyber) for key exchange. Use hybrid X25519+ML-KEM during transition.

_source.reason: DEPRECATED: DSA is obsolete (FIPS 186-5 dropped DSA for new signatures). Also quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace DSA with Ed25519 immediately, then plan ML-DSA migration.

_source.reason: QUANTUM VULNERABLE: Diffie-Hellman broken by Shor's algorithm. Also vulnerable to Logjam with small parameters.
_source.migration: Replace with ECDH (X25519) as interim step, then ML-KEM for full PQC.

_source.reason: QUANTUM VULNERABLE: Based on discrete logarithm problem, broken by Shor's algorithm.
_source.migration: Replace with ML-KEM (Kyber) for encryption.

_source.reason: Modern ECC signature — current best practice for classical crypto, but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with ML-DSA (Dilithium) or use hybrid Ed25519+ML-DSA.

_source.reason: Stronger ECC signature — good classical security, but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with ML-DSA (Dilithium) or use hybrid Ed448+ML-DSA.

_source.reason: Modern ECDH curve — current best practice, but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 for quantum safety.

_source.reason: Stronger ECDH curve — good classical security, but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with hybrid X448+ML-KEM-1024 for quantum safety.

_source.reason: NIST P-256 curve — widely deployed but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with X25519+ML-KEM hybrid.

_source.reason: NIST P-384 curve — stronger classical, but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with P-384+ML-KEM-1024 hybrid.

_source.reason: NIST P-521 curve — strongest NIST curve, but quantum-vulnerable.
_source.migration: Replace with ML-KEM-1024 based key exchange.

_source.reason: Bitcoin/Ethereum curve — quantum-vulnerable. Critical for blockchain applications.
_source.migration: Blockchain layer must adopt PQC signatures. Monitor NIST PQC standardisation for curve replacements.

_source.reason: NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM). Lattice-based KEM — the primary standard for post-quantum key exchange.
_source.migration: Already PQC. Consider ML-KEM-768 as the default security level.

variants.reason: ML-KEM-768: NIST Level 3 (192-bit quantum security) — RECOMMENDED

_source.reason: NIST FIPS 204 (ML-DSA). Lattice-based signature — the primary standard for post-quantum signatures.
_source.migration: Already PQC. Consider ML-DSA-65 as the default security level.

_source.reason: NIST FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA). Hash-based signature — no lattice assumptions, most conservative PQC.
_source.migration: Already PQC. Large signatures — use for root-of-trust, not bulk signing.

_source.reason: NIST-selected PQC signature. Compact signatures but complex implementation (NTRU lattice + FFT).
_source.migration: Already PQC. Prefer ML-DSA for general use; Falcon for size-constrained applications.

_source.reason: One of the oldest lattice-based schemes. Not NIST-standardised but well-studied.
_source.migration: Consider migrating to ML-KEM (Kyber) which is the NIST standard.

_source.reason: NIST PQC Round 3 finalist (not selected for standardisation).
_source.migration: Migrate to ML-KEM (Kyber) which was selected as the NIST standard.

_source.reason: Conservative lattice KEM based on plain LWE (no ring structure). ISO standardised.
_source.migration: FrodoKEM is a valid conservative choice. ML-KEM is faster and NIST-standard.

_source.reason: NIST PQC Round 4 candidate. Code-based KEM.
_source.migration: BIKE is still a candidate. Use ML-KEM for production; BIKE for research/diversity.

_source.reason: NIST PQC Round 4 candidate selected for standardization. Code-based KEM.
_source.migration: HQC is being standardised. Can be used alongside ML-KEM for algorithm diversity.

_source.reason: Stateful hash-based signature. RFC 8391. Quantum-safe with minimal assumptions.
_source.migration: Already PQC. Note: XMSS is STATEFUL — requires careful key management. Use SLH-DSA for stateless needs.

_source.reason: Leighton-Micali hash-based signature. RFC 8554. NIST SP 800-208 approved.
_source.migration: Already PQC. Note: LMS is STATEFUL — requires careful state management.

_source.reason: BROKEN: Key recovery attack by Ward Beullens (2022). Do not use.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace Rainbow with ML-DSA (Dilithium) immediately.

_source.reason: BROKEN: Full key recovery in hours by Castryck-Decru (2022). Do not use.
_source.migration: CRITICAL: Replace SIKE with ML-KEM (Kyber) immediately.

_source.reason: Classic McEliece — oldest unbroken PQC scheme (1978). Extremely large keys but high confidence.
_source.migration: Already PQC. Large keys make it impractical for many use cases. Consider ML-KEM.
